title: P1: standard adopter quality aggregation for hosted snapshots
outOfScope: Publishing a release or creating a version tag.

checkpointPolicy.reason: Record at least one checkpoint before finishing to reduce mid-task drift.

acceptance: The installed Makefile exposes `make quality`, delegating to an explicitly project-owned command or failing closed with a recovery message.
Hosted snapshot preparation rejects a missing or invalid adopter quality configuration before emitting a receipt.
A configured adopter quality command is exercised by the snapshot path and its result is bound to the receipt evidence.
A missing quality configuration regression proves snapshot preparation emits no receipt.
A configured quality command regression proves the installed target delegates successfully.
A malformed configuration regression proves validation fails before command execution.
The English, Japanese, and Simplified-Chinese quality guides name the configuration key and the exact recovery command.
guidelines: Public Make targets and configuration keys must be documented for adopters.
Keep the quality command override project-owned and use list-form process invocation without shell interpolation.
Do not weaken required local or hosted verification to make a missing configuration pass.

intent.problem: #613 records that hosted snapshot guidance requires `make quality` although an installed adopter may not have a standard quality entrypoint; this makes snapshot preparation nondeterministic or impossible.
constraints: Provide an override-friendly aggregate contract rather than hardcoding a repository-specific build tool.
Fail closed with an actionable recovery when the adopter did not configure quality.
Do not publish a release or alter unrelated workflow scheduling in this Work Item.
Record the user's automatic-execution authority in this Contract.
intent.rationale: A template-provided contract gives snapshot and hosted measurement one deterministic verification entrypoint while preserving adopter control of the actual quality command.
